name: Roon
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Rich, Ellora. 2020 [Dec. 2019]. Comparative reconstruction of Proto-Biakic phonology. BA thesis, Swarthmore College (advisor Emily Gasser). 38 pp.
sources.note: Consonant reconstruction for Biak, Roon, Roswar, Dusner; the words stress/accent/prosody do not occur anywhere. States that the Roon data come from fieldwork by Gasser & Gil (2016) and cites Gil 2010 'Word classes in Roon' (unpublished).

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily & David Gil. 2016. Roon Talking Dictionary, version 9.2016. Swarthmore College.https://talkingdictionary.swarthmore.edu/roon/
sources.note: About 340 entries with audio and broad IPA (speaker Jim Betay); no stress marks in any transcription, no orthography/phonology notes page found.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2018. VRK mutation: distribution of a crazy rule in Cenderawasih Bay. Slides, 14-ICAL, Antananarivo.
sources.note: Consonant-mutation slides; Roon appears once (nasal+obstruent examples); no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2017. Tone and language contact in southern Cenderawasih Bay. NUSA 62: 7-39.
sources.note: Moor, Yerisiam, Yaur tone and the Proto-SHWNG penultimate-stress hypothesis; Roon is not mentioned.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2015. The reconstruction of Proto-SHWNG morphology. Paper, 13-ICAL, Taipei.
sources.note: Roon pronoun and agreement paradigms only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David C. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. 263 pp.
sources.note: Comparative work, not a Roon description. Ch. 5 fn. 1 (p. 95): Roon 'may have some kind of tonal contrast' but data are insufficient; Anceaux (n.d.) transcribes Roon [βaˈɾaːna] 'my arm' vs [βaˈɾana] 'his/her arm' (penultimate stress mark, length possibly a misread tone contrast). §5.4 (pp. 116-117): penultimate stress is the default in most described SHWNG languages (list does not include Roon); Proto-SHWNG penultimate stress proposed. No Roon stress rule stated. Roon data sources: Gil (2008) talk and Anceaux (n.d.) notebook.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record roon1237 (JSON) and Wikipedia 'Roon language' (en, id); Wikipedia 'Biakic languages' and 'South Halmahera-West New Guinea languages' reference lists
sources.note: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Deres 2011 (phonology) plus wordlists only (Smits & Voorhoeve 1992, Voorhoeve 1975, Galis 1955, Latham 1862, Fabritius 1855). Wikipedia pages have no phonology section; they supplied the Kamholz and Rich links.

sources.citation: Gil, David. 2008. Some aspects of the grammar of Roon. Talk, MPI-EVA Leipzig; Gil, David. 2010. Word classes in Roon (unpublished); Gil's Roon field notes (basis of Gasser & Gil 2016 Roon Talking Dictionary).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only recent first-hand grammatical work on Roon (Kamholz 2014 and Rich 2020 both draw their Roon data from Gil); a grammar overview would state the stress pattern. Obtainable only from the author (MPI-EVA) or Emily Gasser (Swarthmore).

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2024. Historical linguistics of the South Halmahera-West New Guinea subgroup. In Adelaar & Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, 181-187. Oxford: OUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Latest overview of SHWNG by the author who holds the Roon data; may update the 2014 remark on Roon tone/stress. Short and comparative, so unlikely to give a Roon rule.

sources.citation: Deres, Ongen Nover. 2011. Phonemic inventory of Roon as spoken in Yende. MA thesis, Universitas Negeri Papua (UNIPA), Manokwari. xxiii+94 pp.

sources.note: The only phonological description of Roon in Glottolog (listed by Glottolog as a phonology); a phonemic-inventory thesis normally has a suprasegmentals section giving the stress pattern. Hammarström's bibliography records the page count, so a copy exists outside UNIPA.
